recon.notes: WordPress + The Events Calendar (Tribe) 6.17.3, confirmed by the working /wp-json/tribe/events/v1/events endpoint and the ICS PRODID. REST rows carry no series key and no recurrence field, yet 20 titles repeat on a fixed cadence and each recurring title has a Tribe /all/ index (Chub Rub verified) — the site runs Tribe recurrence with per-occurrence rows. Weekly titles (Shirts Off Sundays, PILLOWS) are only pre-expanded ~6 weeks ahead (last row 2026-10-26); monthly titles 2–3 months ahead. Cadence text, where the site publishes it, is in the description ("Every Third Saturday", "Every 4th Friday", "Every First Saturday", "Every first Sunday!", "every second Wednesday", "every third Wednesday", "Every FIRST WEDNESDAY", "The Monday drag party"); nine repeating titles publish no cadence text and are grouped from their dates with the occurrence-URL quoted as the structural statement. All 57 rows are at the bar itself (1347 Folsom St) with real coordinates. The 2026-09-12 trial run kept 3 records (Chub Rub ×2, FLEX) and bear-dropped 54.

coverage.basis: REST feed page 1 (total 57, total_pages 2) + page 2 from the scraper page cache = 57 rows, 57 distinct ids, Sep 11 2026 – Feb 24 2027. The configured /events/ list shows the first 12 of them statically and links pages 2–3; the ICS export carries 30 of them (Sep 12 – Oct 12) with identical wall-clock times; zero conflicts between doors. Collapse: 20 titles repeat on a provable cadence (2 weekly, 18 monthly nth-weekday; 50 rows) → 20 series; 7 rows are one-offs or unprovable pairs (Rubber Ducky, FLEX, Black Brown and Kinky, NUTZ, SHAGGIN, The Playpen ×2) → 7 singles. publishedEventCount = 27. Every occurrence is a dated feed row (origin listed); the window end 2026-12-31 exceeds every listed series date, and no rule-derived dates are added beyond what the site lists. Past listings: the list view links a "Previous Events" view (/events/list/?eventDisplay=past) and the Chub Rub /all/ index shows one past instance (2026-05-16); the past view itself was not read (no request budget), so the count is unknown.
knownGaps: The past view (/events/list/?eventDisplay=past) was not read; how many past rows the site keeps is unknown (REST with start_date=2000-01-01 would answer it in one call).
Weekly series occurrences stop where the feed's pre-expansion stops (2026-10-25 Shirts Off Sundays, 2026-10-26 PILLOWS); November–December Sundays/Mondays are not asserted.
Event-page descriptions were taken from REST; only two occurrence pages (t-dance 2026-09-11, chub-rub /all/) were opened.

traps.label: "T – Dance" and "Cuir" on 2026-09-11 — the first two REST rows, already over at recon
traps.why: REST's server-set start_date is 2026-09-11 02:00:00, so the feed still returns Friday's two parties on Saturday; the HTML list and the ICS export both start at Sep 12. Extracting them is correct under allowPastEvents (they are real instances of the T – Dance and Cuir series), but they must keep their Sep 11 date.

traps.label: "Events from September 12 – September 25" + rel-next /events/page/2/, /events/page/3/ on the configured list page
traps.why: The static list page holds only 12 of the 57 rows. A run that reads just the configured HTML without following pagination (or without the REST door) sees two weeks of programming and misses the other 45 rows — a coverage trap rather than a false event. The pagination links themselves are not events.

traps.label: /event/chub-rub/all/ lists "2026-05-16" alongside the two upcoming Chub Rub dates
traps.why: Tribe's per-series index shows every occurrence including past ones. Reachable only by crawling from an occurrence page; if the crawl follows it, the May 16 instance appears as a past record (legitimate under allowPastEvents) — it is not a third upcoming Chub Rub.

expect.note: Depends on whether the crawl follows the /all/ link from an occurrence page; the configured list and the REST door never expose it.

traps.label: "Previous Events" link → /events/list/?eventDisplay=past
traps.why: The past archive of a Tribe site; not read during recon. Rows behind it are already-happened instances of the same series and must not be counted as upcoming.

expect.note: Not read; whether the crawl follows the past view is a config question (allowPastEvents), not a site one.

openQuestions.q: Nine repeating titles (T – Dance, Cuir, HOUSE PARTY, Shirts Off Sundays, PRIMAL, Chub Rub, Cocktailgate, Carne Fresca, Fan-Dumb, TRAVIESO) publish no cadence text; the rules here are proven from 2–7 listed dates plus Tribe's date-suffixed occurrence URLs. If the scraper should only ever write a recurrence it can quote, these stay dated singles per occurrence.
The 2026-09-12 trial run bear-dropped 54 of 57 records including Chub Rub-adjacent bear/leather programming (BEATPIG, Stank, LICK IT, FLEX kept). Bear verdicts are deferred to the owner's pass.
